citation.authors: Baird DD, Dunson DB, Hill MC, Cousins D et al
citation.journal: American Journal of Obstetrics and Gynecology

record.population: 1,364 randomly selected women aged 35-49 in a US urban health plan (Black and White)
record.design: Ultrasound screening plus records, estimating cumulative incidence of fibroids by age
record.finding: By age 50, cumulative incidence of fibroids was above 80% for Black women and nearly 70% for White women (odds ratio 2.9, 95% CI 2.5-3.4). Fibroids developed at earlier ages in Black women. Fifty-one percent of premenopausal women with no previous diagnosis had ultrasound evidence of fibroids.
